title: Johnson–Lindenstrauss embedding from a Gaussian matrix
statement:
Fix dimensions $d$ and $k$ with $k \ge 1$, a distortion parameter $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$, and a finite set of points $V \subseteq \bbr^d$. Let $A$ be a random $k \times d$ matrix whose entries $A_{ij}$ are independent Gaussian random variables, each with mean $0$ and variance $1/k$. If the union-bound quantity satisfies
\[
  |V|^2 \cdot 2\exp\!\left(-\,k\varepsilon^2/8\right) < 1,
\]
then there exists a linear map $f : \bbr^d \to \bbr^k$ that is an $\varepsilon$-JL embedding of $V$: for every pair $u, v \in V$,
\[
  (1-\varepsilon)\,\|u-v\|^2 \;\le\; \|f(u)-f(v)\|^2 \;\le\; (1+\varepsilon)\,\|u-v\|^2.
\]
hypotheses_covered: A is a random k×d matrix with entries ~ N(0, 1/k)
entries within each row are independent
the rows of A are independent
V is a finite subset of ℝ^d
replaced:
